description:
The Relation Grid (RFC 0050 · Episode 2), as its own project. A grid
        that captures intents and ARRANGES cells, and holds no value: a
        relation is identities, columns and a cell manager, the domain owns
        every cell for its whole life, and edit, commit and update are the
        domain's operations that never change an arrangement.

        rel-channel is the ask channel's core — a notification handed over, a
        question waited on behind the mask — the family's, under a surface.
        rel-grid-protocol is the ask protocol: every question and answer
        declared once as a Java record, its JS class generated at build time.

        rel-grid-selection is the selection: an ordered list of ranges over
        positions, in a module that imports nothing at all.

        rel-grid is the primitive — plain JS classes with no runtime
        dependency on anything, packaged as homing DomModules for this stack.
        rel-tree is the tree view (Episode 3): the second component on the
        same doctrine, over the channel and the protocol and nothing of the grid.
        json-kit is the first out-of-the-box offering: a JSON viewer on the tree
        view — domain-side code that ships, holding values as any domain does.
        rel-grid-workbench is the solo studio of benches that try to make it
        fail, on the workspace shell.
